summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, chronic hepatitis C cirrhosis, and high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for her third cycle of doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy. She tolerated treatment well with minimal nausea, supported by scheduled antiemetics including dexamethasone, ondansetron, and lorazepam. Due to a prior leukemoid reaction from Neulasta, she was transitioned to Neupogen, to be started 48 hours after chemotherapy completion. Her hemoglobin dropped to 6.6 g/dL, prompting a transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with no signs of infection or sickle cell crisis. Liver enzymes improved during admission, and her pain was well controlled with hydromorphone. She was discharged home with clear instructions on medication management, infection precautions, and follow-up care.
problems: Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Malignant neoplasm of long bones of lower limb
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
